newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay backs high Thai rates to curb speculation.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay backs high Thai rates to curb speculation.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Friday he backed a central bank policy to induce high Thai interest rates as a measure to curb speculation against the weak Thai baht.

The minister said the Bank of Thailand should closely monitor volatile interbank rates and keep them high on some days to maintain proper money market liquidity and discourage speculation against the baht.

"The central bank has been asked to watch interbank rates closely. It would keep them high on some days depending on which direction it wants liquidity to flow so as to curb excessive speculation (on the baht)," he said.
"We sometimes need to apply the whip on speculators moving against the baht," Amnuay said.

The overnight interbank rate soared to a six-month high of 25-26 percent early on Friday amid the seasonal high-spending Chinese Lunar New Year and on demand for baht from some players to buy the surging dollar, dealers said.
Amnuay reiterated his earlier assurances that Thailand had no plan to change its practice of fixing the baht against a basket of major foreign currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.
He said although the baht has sharply depreciated against a surging dollar in recent weeks, it had rallied against the yen and mark.
The minister said despite recent baht volatility, the Thai currency still retained its economic and trade competitiveness compared with some other Asian countries.

The baht's current softness against the dollar aggravated a prolonged slump of the Thai stock market which sank to its 4-1/2 year low this week. Foreign stock investors tried to trim foreign exchange losses by switching from baht-denominated Thai stocks to assets kept in dollars, dealers said.
